problem.paragraph: $$\iint_{R}{ye^{\mathit{xy}}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $${R = \left\{ {\left( {x,y} \right)|0 \leqslant x \leqslant 2} \right.},{0 \leqslant \left. {y \leqslant 3} \right\}}$$
$$\iint_{D}{xy\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $${D = \left\{ {\left( {x,y} \right)|0 \leqslant y \leqslant 1} \right.},{y^{2} \leqslant x \leqslant \left. {y + 2} \right\}}$$
$$\iint\limits_{D}{\frac{y}{1 + x^{2}}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$D$$ is bounded by $$y = \sqrt{x}$$ , $$y = 0$$ , $$x = 1$$
$$\iint\limits_{D}{\frac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$D$$ is the triangular region with vertices $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1,1} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {0,1} \right)$$
$$\iint_{D}{y\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$D$$ is the region in the first quadrant bounded by the parabolas $$x = y^{2}$$ and $$x = 8 - y^{2}$$
$$\iint_{D}{y\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$D$$ is the region in the first quadrant that lies above the hyperbola $$xy = 1$$ and the line $$y = x$$ and below the line $$y = 2$$
$$\iint_{D}{{({x^{2} + y^{2}})}^{3 \slash 2}\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$D$$ is the region in the first quadrant bounded by the lines $$y = 0$$ and $$y = \sqrt{3}x$$ and the circle $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 9$$
$$\iint_{D}{x\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$D$$ is the region in the first quadrant that lies between the circles $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ and $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 2$$
$$\iiint_{E}{xy\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $${E = \left\{ {\left( {x,y,z} \right)|0 \leqslant x \leqslant 3,} \right.}0{\leqslant y \leqslant x,}{0 \leqslant z \leqslant \left. {x + y} \right\}}$$

$$\iiint_{T}{xy\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$T$$ is the solid tetrahedron with vertices $$\left( {0,0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {\frac{1}{3},0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,1,0} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {0,0,1} \right)$$
$$\iiint_{E}{y^{2}z^{2}\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$E$$ is bounded by the paraboloid $$x = 1 - y^{2} - z^{2}$$ and the plane $$x = 0$$
$$\iiint_{E}{z\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$E$$ is bounded by the planes $$y = 0$$ , $$z = 0$$ , $$x + y = 2$$ and the cylinder $$y^{2} + z^{2} = 1$$ in the first octant
$$\iiint_{E}{yz\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$E$$ lies above the plane $$z = 0$$ , below the plane $$z = y$$ , and inside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$$
$${\iiint_{H}{z^{3}\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}}}dV$$ , where $$H$$ is the solid hemisphere that lies above the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane and has center the origin and radius $$1$$

exercises.instruction: 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, and 40 Find the volume of the given solid.

problem.paragraph: Under the paraboloid $$z = x^{2} + 4y^{2}$$ and above the rectangle $$R = \left\lbrack {0,2} \right\rbrack \times \left\lbrack {1,4} \right\rbrack$$
Under the surface $$z = x^{2}y$$ and above the triangle in the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane with vertices $$\left( {1,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {2,1} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {4,0} \right)$$
The solid tetrahedron with vertices $$\left( {0,0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,0,1} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,2,0} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {2,2,0} \right)$$
Bounded by the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$$ and the planes $$z = 0$$ and $$y + z = 3$$
One of the wedges cut from the cylinder $$x^{2} + 9y^{2} = a^{2}$$ by the planes $$z = 0$$ and $$z = mx$$
Above the paraboloid $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ and below the half-cone $$z = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$
Consider a lamina that occupies the region $$D$$ bounded by the parabola $$x = 1 - y^{2}$$ and the coordinate axes in the first quadrant with density function $$\rho\left( {x,y} \right) = y$$ .

list.item: Find the mass of the lamina.
Find the center of mass.
Find the moments of inertia and radii of gyration about the $$x$$ - and $$y$$ -axes.

problem.paragraph: A lamina occupies the part of the disk $$x^{2} + y^{2} \leqslant a^{2}$$ that lies in the first quadrant.

list.item: Find the centroid of the lamina.
Find the center of mass of the lamina if the density function is $$\rho\left( {x,y} \right) = xy^{2}$$ .

Find the centroid of a solid right circular cone with height $$h$$ and base radius $$a$$ . (Place the cone so that its base is in the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane with center the origin and its axis along the positive $$z$$ -axis.)
If the cone has density function $$\rho\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$ , find the moment of inertia of the cone about its axis (the $$z$$ -axis).

problem.paragraph: Find the area of the part of the cone $$z^{2} = a^{2}{({x^{2} + y^{2}})}$$ between the planes $$z = 1$$ and $$z = 2$$ .
Find the area of the part of the surface $$z = x^{2} + y$$ that lies above the triangle with vertices $$(0,0)$$ , $$(1,0)$$ , and $$(0,2)$$ .
Use a computer algebra system to graph the surface $$z = x\sin y$$ , $$- 3 \leqslant x \leqslant 3$$ , $$- \pi \leqslant y \leqslant \pi$$ and find its surface area correct to four decimal places.
Use polar coordinates to evaluate
Use spherical coordinates to evaluate

If $$D$$ is the region bounded by the curves $$y = 1 - x^{2}$$ and $$y = e^{ x}$$ , find the approximate value of the integral $$\iint_{D}{y^{2}\mathit{dA}}$$ . (Use a graph to estimate the points of intersection of the curves.)

Use a computer algebra system to find the center of mass of the solid tetrahedron with vertices $$\left( {0,0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1,0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,2,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,0,3} \right)$$ and density function $$\rho\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}$$ .
The joint density function for random variables $$X$$ and $$Y$$ is
$$f(x,y) = \begin{cases} {C(x + y)} & {{if}0 \leqslant x \leqslant 3,0 \leqslant y \leqslant 2} \\ 0 & {otherwise} \end{cases}$$

list.item: Find the value of the constant $$C$$ .
Find $$P\left( {X \leqslant 2,Y \geqslant 1} \right)$$ .
Find $$P\left( {X + Y \leqslant 1} \right)$$ .

problem.paragraph: A lamp has three bulbs, each of a type with average lifetime $$800$$ hours. If we model the probability of failure of a bulb by an exponential density function with mean $$800$$ , find the probability that all three bulbs fail within a total of $$1000$$ hours.
Rewrite the integral
$$\int_{- 1}^{1}{\int_{x^{2}}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1 - y}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dz}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dx}}}}$$
as an iterated integral in the order $$\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dz}$$ .
Give five other iterated integrals that are equal to
$$\int_{0}^{2}{\int_{0}^{y^{3}}{\int_{0}^{y^{2}}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dz}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}}}}$$
Use the transformation $$u = x - y$$ , $$\upsilon = x + y$$ to evaluate
$$\iint\limits_{R}{\frac{x - y}{x + y}\mathit{dA}}$$
where $$R$$ is the square with vertices $$\left( {0,2} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1,1} \right)$$ , $$\left( {2,2} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {1,3} \right)$$ .
Use the transformation $$x = u^{2}$$ , $$y = \upsilon^{2}$$ , $$z = w^{2}$$ to find the volume of the region bounded by the surface $$\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z} = 1$$ and the coordinate planes.

Use the change of variables formula and an appropriate transformation to evaluate $$\iint_{R}{xy\mathit{dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the square with vertices $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1,1} \right)$$ , $$\left( {2,0} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {1, - 1} \right)$$ .

list.item: Evaluate $$\iint\limits_{D}{\frac{1}{{({x^{2} + y^{2}})}^{n \slash 2}}\mathit{dA}}$$ where $$n$$ is an integer and $$D$$ is the region bounded by the circles with center the origin and radii $$r$$ and $$R$$ , $$0 < r < R$$ .
For what values of $$n$$ does the integral in part (a) have a limit as $$\left. r\rightarrow 0^{+} \right.$$ ?

Find $$\iiint\limits_{E}{\frac{1}{{({x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}})}^{n \slash 2}}\mathit{dV}}$$ where $$E$$ is the region bounded by the spheres with center the origin and radii $$r$$ and $$R$$ , $$0 < r < R$$ .
For what values of $$n$$ does the integral in part (c) have a limit as $$\left. r\rightarrow 0^{+} \right.$$ ?

section.heading: Problems Plus

list.item: 1. If $$〚x〛$$ denotes the greatest integer in $$x$$ , evaluate the integral $${\iint\limits_{R}{〚{x + y}〛}}\mathit{dA}$$ where $$R = \left\{ {\left( {x,y} \right)|1 \leqslant x \leqslant 3,2 \leqslant y \leqslant 5} \right\}$$ . $$30$$

2. Evaluate the integral $$\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1}{e^{\max{\{{x^{2},y^{2}}\}}}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dx}}}$$ where $$\max\left\{ {x^{2},y^{2}} \right\}$$ means the larger of the numbers $$x^{2}$$ and $$y^{2}$$ .
3. Find the average value of the function $$f(x) = {\int_{x}^{1}{\cos{(t^{2})}dt}}$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {0,1} \right\rbrack$$ . $$\frac{1}{2}\sin 1$$

5. The double integral $$\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1}{\frac{1}{1 - xy}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}}}$$ is an improper integral and could be defined as the limit of double integrals over the rectangle $$\left\lbrack {0,t} \right\rbrack \times \left\lbrack {0,t} \right\rbrack$$ as $$\left. t\rightarrow 1^{-} \right.$$ . But if we expand the integrand as a geometric series, we can express the integral as the sum of an infinite series. Show that $$\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1}{\frac{1}{1 - xy}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy} = \sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^{2}}}}$$

6. Leonhard Euler was able to find the exact sum of the series in Problem 5. In 1736 he proved that $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}{\frac{1}{n^{2}} = \frac{\pi^{2}}{6}}$$ In this problem we ask you to prove this fact by evaluating the double integral in Problem 5. Start by making the change of variables $${x = \frac{u - \upsilon}{\sqrt{2}}} {y = \frac{u + \upsilon}{\sqrt{2}}}$$ This gives a rotation about the origin through the angle $$\pi \slash 4$$ . You will need to sketch the corresponding region in the $$u\upsilon$$ -plane. [Hint: If, in evaluating the integral, you encounter either of the expressions $$\left( {1 - \sin\theta} \right) \slash \cos\theta$$ or $$\left( {\cos\theta} \right) \slash \left( {1 + \sin\theta} \right)$$ , you might like to use the identity $$\cos\theta = \sin\left( {\left( {\pi \slash 2} \right) - \theta} \right)$$ and the corresponding identity for $$\sin\theta$$ .]

7. Show that $$\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1}{\frac{1}{1 - xyz}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dz} = \sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^{3}}}}}$$ (Nobody has ever been able to find the exact value of the sum of this series.) Show that $$\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1}{\frac{1}{1 + xyz}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dz} = \sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}\frac{\left( {- 1} \right)^{n - 1}}{n^{3}}}}}$$ Use this equation to evaluate the triple integral correct to two decimal places. $$0.90$$
8. Show that $$\int_{0}^{\infty}{\frac{\arctan\pi x - \arctan x}{x}\mathit{dx} = \frac{\pi}{2}\ln\pi}$$ by first expressing the integral as an iterated integral.

9. Show that when Laplace’s equation $$\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial x^{2}} + \frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial y^{2}} + \frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial z^{2}} = 0$$ is written in cylindrical coordinates, it becomes $$\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial r^{2}} + \frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial u}{\partial r} + \frac{1}{r^{2}}\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial\theta^{2}} + \frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial z^{2}} = 0$$ Show that when Laplace’s equation is written in spherical coordinates, it becomes $$\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial\rho^{2}} + \frac{2}{\rho}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\rho} + \frac{\cot\phi}{\rho^{2}}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\phi} + \frac{1}{\rho^{2}}\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial\phi^{2}} + \frac{1}{\rho^{2}\sin^{2}\phi}\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial\theta^{2}} = 0$$

10. A lamina has constant density $$\rho$$ and takes the shape of a disk with center the origin and radius $$R$$ . Use Newton’s Law of Gravitation (see Section 13.4) to show that the magnitude of the force of attraction that the lamina exerts on a body with mass $$m$$ located at the point $$\left( {0,0,d} \right)$$ on the positive $$z$$ -axis is $$F = 2\pi Gm\rho d\left( {\frac{1}{d} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{R^{2} + d^{2}}}} \right)$$ [Hint: Divide the disk as in Figure 15.3.4 and first compute the vertical component of the force exerted by the polar subrectangle $$R_{ij}$$ .] Show that the magnitude of the force of attraction of a lamina with density $$\rho$$ that occupies an entire plane on an object with mass $$m$$ located at a distance $$d$$ from the plane is $$F = 2\pi Gm\rho$$ Notice that this expression does not depend on $$d$$ .
11. If $$f$$ is continuous, show that $$\int_{0}^{x}{\int_{0}^{y}{\int_{0}^{z}{f(t)dt\mathit{dz}\mathit{dy} = \frac{1}{2}{\int_{0}^{x}{\left( {x - t} \right)^{2}f{(t)}dt}}}}}$$
12. Evaluate $$\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}n^{- 2}\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{n}\sum\limits_{j = 1}^{n^{2}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^{2} + ni + j}}$$ .

13. The plane $${\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} + \frac{z}{c} = 1 }{a > 0,}{b > 0,}{c > 0}$$ cuts the solid ellipsoid $$\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} + \frac{z^{2}}{c^{ 2}} \leqslant 1$$ into two pieces. Find the volume of the smaller piece. $$abc\pi\left( {\frac{2}{3} - \frac{8}{9\sqrt{3}}} \right)$$
